visuals.title: Where it happens
visuals.text: Infection climbs from the bladder and urethra to the epididymis and testis; mumps arrives from the parotid via the blood.

glossary.Testis: The male gonad that produces sperm and testosterone; plural testes.
glossary.Klebsiella pneumoniae: A Gram-negative gut bacterium that causes urinary and other infections.
glossary.Mumps virus: Paramyxovirus causing parotitis, which can spread to the testes.
glossary.Urinary pathogens: Bacteria that usually cause urinary tract infection, chiefly E. coli.
glossary.Unprotected intercourse: Sex without a condom, the main risk for sexually transmitted infection.
glossary.Catheterisation: Passing a tube into the bladder to drain urine.
glossary.Scrotal: Relating to the scrotum, the skin sac holding the testes.
glossary.Erythematous: Red, from increased blood flow due to inflammation.
glossary.Erythema: Redness of the skin from inflammation.
glossary.Palpable: Able to be felt on examination.
glossary.Parotid gland: The large salivary gland in front of the ear, which swells in mumps.
glossary.Unvaccinated: Not having received a vaccine, here the MMR.
glossary.Infertility: Inability to conceive after a year of regular unprotected sex.
glossary.Testicular abscess: A collection of pus within the testis needing drainage.
glossary.Urine culture: Growing bacteria from urine to identify the organism and its antibiotic sensitivities.
glossary.Mid-stream urine: Urine caught midway through passing, to reduce contamination from the skin.
glossary.Microscopy: Looking at a sample under a microscope for cells and bacteria.
glossary.Urethral swab: A sample taken from inside the urethra to test for infection.
glossary.Gonorrhoea: Sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
glossary.Chlamydia: The commonest bacterial sexually transmitted infection in the UK.
glossary.Scrotal elevation: Supporting the scrotum, e.g. with tight underwear, to ease pain.
glossary.Supportive treatment: Care that relieves symptoms while the body recovers.
glossary.Contiguously: By direct spread into neighbouring tissue.
glossary.BPH: Benign prostatic hyperplasia: non-cancerous prostate enlargement that obstructs urine flow.
glossary.Outflow obstruction: Blockage to urine leaving the bladder, e.g. from an enlarged prostate.
glossary.Stasis: Stagnation of a fluid, here urine, which encourages infection.
glossary.Venous congestion: Pooling of blood in the veins, causing swelling and pain.
glossary.Vascular pedicle: The stalk carrying the blood supply to an organ, here the spermatic cord.
glossary.Ischaemic: Starved of blood supply and oxygen.
